newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda forecasts lower coffee earnings in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Uganda forecasts lower coffee earnings in 1996/97.

text.p: Uganda, Africa's leading coffee exporter, has forecast a further drop in export earnings in line with expected low world prices and a decline in its own supply.

The Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) projected exports to decline to 3.6 million 60 kg (132.3 lb) bags in 1996/97 from a record 4.15 million bags in 1995/96 and forecast earnings down to $296.16 million from $388.92 million in 1995/96.
The UCDA blamed the lower projections on hail stones in some key growing districts around August 1996 and a coffee disease.
It said the coffee wilt disease had affected some plantations especially in southwest and central Uganda.
The authority projected exporter closing stocks at 357,000 bags in 1996/97 from 225,978 bags in 1995/96 (October/September).

The UCDA predicted volume of exports at 674,080 bags in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October-December) with earnings at $55.042 million. That compared with 795,502 bags worth $88.051 million in the same quarter of the previous crop year.
But the UCDA gave the impression it was happy with farmer activity.

"On the whole, farmers countrywide continued to tend their coffee trees in response to the good prices arising from the cut-throat competition within the industry and the Brazilian frost of 1994," the UCDA said.
"Farmers' efforts were further given support by the exceptionally good weather throughout the year," the UCDA added.

Besides the price incentives, the UCDA said the increase in farm level production was due to the replacement of the less productive old trees with an early maturing clonal variety planted three to four years ago.
"Replacement is planned to be done at the rate of 5.0 percent per annum and it is hoped that within 20 years, from 1991/92, 240,000 hectares (593,040 acres) shall have been replanted," the UCDA said.
In explaining an expected price fall, the UCDA said:
"Present indications are that there is likely to be more than enough coffee from origins to cover roaster demand adequately for the season."

"This is based on reported increases in production from major growing countries such as Brazil, Indonesia, Uganda and Vietnam. The consumption level, on the other hand, has had no significant corresponding increase," the UCDA added.

The UCDA said increased supply of Brazilian quality coffee, estimated at 24-26 million bags, could adversely affect demand for replacement coffees which sustained the industry during the past 15 months when Brazil was absent from the market.

It said prices were also likely to keep low, although with some short recoveries, due to speculative tendencies by investment funds, liquidation and higher availability towards the end of the year when harvesting is at peak among growers.
The UCDA said Uganda would be greatly affected by a fall in international prices that will result from high production of the robusta variety, estimated at 30 million bags in 1996/97.
